![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196632/assets/09ea9b27d573f7ca318e00a912a18d6c8de8b66ead5c85fb90ebea7f5bd20ca8.png)

Given that the point $A$ has coordinates $(2\sqrt{3},-6),$ calculate the angle $\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
We can form a triangle by creating a vertical line from $A$ to the $x$-axis. Let us call ${\theta }^{′}$ the angle that is formed with the $x$-axis such that ${\theta }^{′}+\theta =2\pi $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196632/assets/eb659af0765e200333ca35b716772d92765c7f46ccc4b267243b3c82ba88a1e8.png)

Using the tangent ratio, we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡{\theta }^{′}=\frac{6}{2\sqrt{3}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3}.
$$

Finally, using the inverse tangent, we get

$$
{\theta }^{′}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3}=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Finally, using $\theta +{\theta }^{′}=2\pi ,$ we get $\theta =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{5\pi }{3}.$
